item.title: Code Blocks, Captions, and Other Hugo Tricks
item.dc:creator: Your Name
item.description: A quick tour of the Markdown features this theme adds on top of plain Hugo.
item.content:encoded:
The Kana theme does not change how you write Markdown, but it does add a few helpful extras. Here are the ones I use most.

Syntax highlighting with a filename

Add a file attribute to a fenced code block and the theme will label it:

main.go
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    fmt.Println("Hello from a Hugo code block")
}

The highlighting uses the Gruvbox palette.

Collapsible code blocks

Long snippets can be folded away with details=true:

Details
hugo new content posts/2026/my-new-post.md
hugo server --buildDrafts
hugo --minify

Responsive images

Images placed in assets/ can be inserted with the asset-image shortcode, which handles WebP conversion and sizing for you:

{{< asset-image "images/dev-image-03.jpeg" "600" "400" "A caption" >}}

That’s it

Everything else is standard Markdown. Headings, lists, links, blockquotes, tables — they all just work.

item.title: Why I Write
item.dc:creator: Your Name
item.description: Some thoughts on keeping a blog in an age of infinite feeds.
item.content:encoded:
I write to think. There is something about putting a half-formed idea into sentences that forces me to notice where the idea is actually hollow.

Writing as a filter

When a thought stays in my head, it feels complete. The moment I try to write it down, the gaps show up. Writing is how I separate the ideas that survive contact with a keyboard from the ones that only sounded good at 2 a.m.

Owning the words

A blog I own is different from a post on someone else’s platform. There is no engagement metric here, no algorithmic timeline deciding who sees this. That freedom changes what I’m willing to say.

The best reason to write on your own site is that nobody can take it away from you.

If you’re considering starting a blog, my advice is simply: start. Write the first post badly, publish it, and fix it later.

item.title: Welcome to the Blog
item.dc:creator: Your Name
item.description: A short hello and a look at what this site is going to be.
item.content:encoded:
Hello, and welcome. This is the first post on a brand-new blog, which means it is mostly a promise about what comes next rather than a finished thing.

What to expect

I plan to write here about three broad topics:

  1. Software — things I build, tools I like, and lessons learned the hard way.
  2. Books — short reactions to what I’m reading, tracked in the library.
  3. Notes — quick, half-formed thoughts that don’t deserve a full post.

How this site is built

This site is generated with Hugo using the Kana theme. That means every page you read started life as a Markdown file. Writing a post is as simple as creating a new file and running the dev server.

If you’d like to follow along, subscribe to the RSS feed. See you in the next one.
